messages:
jamie: quick FYI — noticed a regression on h100 for seq=128 where the router prefers Triton and p50 jumps. attaching notes.

sanjay: can you paste the profile snippet? curious if it's kernel-launch overhead or a bad cuBLAS path. :thinking:

jamie: pprof + perf sample. short version: when chosen=triton at seq=128 we see p50 ~34ms (was ~12ms with CUTLASS). tokens/sec drops ~45k -> ~18k. GPU util drops too.

lee: dropping the raw lines from the probe log:
```
[kernel_choice] model=gpt-like-7b seq=64 batch=1 chosen=cutlass latency=11.8ms
[kernel_choice] model=gpt-like-7b seq=128 batch=1 chosen=triton latency=33.9ms
[kv_cache] hit_rate=0.82 probe_mode=warm
[gpu] util=72% -> 56% when triton chosen
```

melissa: interesting — KV cache warm hits are non-zero so not purely coldstart. could be that Triton microkernel increases launch count or forces different memory layout that reduces occupancy.

jamie: my hypothesis: Triton's fused kernels here have worse handling for the specific attention tiling we use at seq=128 on H100 (smaller effective batch due to KV shaping) which increases kernel-launch-to-exec ratio. CUTLASS uses a different matmul path that stays in high-throughput GEMM.

sanjay: do we have autotuner traces for that model+hw combo? want to see candidate scores it produced (latency vs mem).

lee: grabbed the autotune dump from the canary:
```json
{
 "candidates": [
  {"id": "cutlass_v1", "score": 1.0, "median_ms": 12.1},
  {"id": "triton_fusedA", "score": 0.85, "median_ms": 13.5},
  {"id": "triton_fusedB", "score": 2.7, "median_ms": 34.0}
 ]
}
```
(note: score is internal cost metric where lower is better; but recent runs show noise for fusedB at seq>=96)

melissa: that fusedB looks like an outlier. maybe the probe sampling for seq128 picked the wrong seed batch (rare distribution) and autotuner didn't explore enough. we should re-run autotune with repeated probes and explicit seq bins.

jamie: agrees. also small but important: router's fallback hysteresis is currently pure-count based (n failures) — we should add seqlen-aware thresholds. e.g. require 3 failing probes at seq>=96 within window before flip.

infra-bot: canary-deploy #325 completed on pool=h100-canary. Telemetry forwarded to #ingest (link).

sanjay: can someone run a targeted A/B: force CUTLASS vs force TRITON for seq in {96,128,192} and capture p50/p95, gpu-util, kv-hit breakdown? I can script the comparison.

lee: volunteering. plan: 1000 requests each seq bucket, mix of batch sizes {1,2,4}, with KV warm/cold toggles. will push results to the perf board.

melissa: add a probe that logs per-kernel-launch count and average runtime — that will help show if it's launch overhead.

jamie: added. sample log format:
```
[kernel_profile] kernel=matmul type=triton launches=42 avg_ms=0.75
[kernel_profile] kernel=matmul type=cutlass launches=6 avg_ms=2.0
```
(suspect Triton has more tiny launches which kills throughput)

lee: quick note from a small run: for seq128 batch1, triton path shows ~38 launches per request, cutlass ~6 launches. avg per-launch small but overhead sums up.

sanjay: OK. actionable items:
- lee: run full A/B and upload raw traces (assign)
- melissa: re-run autotuner with repeated probes and explicit seqlen buckets, and increase exploration for fused kernels
- jamie: add seqlen-aware hysteresis to router config (temp toggle)

melissa: will also test KV-warm vs forced-cold (invalidate every 10 requests) to isolate KV effect.

jamie: one more wrinkle — we saw a regression spike on one customer pool that had a slightly older cuDNN driver; can someone verify driver mismatch sensitivity for Triton fused path?

lee: noted — will reproduce on matching driver and an older one. adding to A/B matrix.

sanjay: thanks team. if A/B confirms, we should rollback the default preference for seq>=96 to CUTLASS until autotuner stabilizes. No reason to risk customer tails. :white_check_mark:

melissa: agree. I'll draft a quick canary rollback plan and post in #eng-releases after we have the traces.

jamie: perfect. will monitor for any knock-on on mem usage. closing thread once traces uploaded.
